messages:
alex: FYI from Sales — Synapse Labs reported a sharp p95 jump after last night's routing tweak. They hit ~980ms p95 and ~10% 5xx on text.generate. They're on Dedicated (reserved). @maria can you triage impact/priority?

maria: thanks, alex. do we have customer id + example request? severity? SLA exposure?

sam-sales: Synapse ID syn-8743. They say spike started ~02:15 UTC after the routing rollout. Example curl they sent: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-2","input":"summarize: ..."}'
```
Errors: intermittent 502/504; CPU on their side high but they say this was correlated with our p95. They're on a 99.9% per-minute p95 SLA for dedicated. Customer is upset and asking for ETA.

maria: can we get metrics? p50/p95/p99, error rate time series, and route config change that rolled out at 02:10? tagging eng.

devon-eng: grabbing logs now. initial look: backend routing fallback to surge-capacity (cheaper variant) started at 02:11 for a small % of tokens. I see queue growth in the dedicated pool, queue latency increased -> backend started failing healthchecks briefly. P95 correlates with fallback events.

kevin-sre: can you paste the serviceroute config diff? Also need kernel/quantization variant used for that model on that pool. If fallback invoked cheaper quantized variant, KV cache mismatch could be adding latency.

sam-sales: attaching customer trace snippet (redacted) and a short timeline they sent. They want a hotfix or rollback.

alex: product question — is this an operational bug we treat as P0 for Synapse (committed SLA) or P1 requiring scheduled patch? Customer asks for mitigation within 4 hours.

maria: we should follow SLA: convert to P0 for this customer. Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) rollback the routing change for dedicated pools -> immediate restore, 2) add a targeted routing rule to prefer non-quant variant for syn-8743, 3) capacity bump for their pool. Need eng signoff.

devon-eng: rollback is simplest and low-risk. I'll open an eng-runtime rollback PR and coordinate with infra for a targeted change. Also will add a canary to avoid flipping everyone. Estimated 60–90m to finish and validate.

kevin-sre: I'll prepare a runbook step to pin their pool to stable kernels and increase healthcheck sensitivity. Also add temporary 10% burst to their dedicated pool.

maria: ok, product action items: create intake ticket with acceptance criteria: (a) p95 back under 300ms within 2 hours, (b) <0.1% 5xx sustained, (c) postmortem with root cause and rollout checklist. We will escalate to customer success and assign account exec.

alex: please also capture launch/rollback criteria so PMs can sign off on re-rollout: e.g., canary thresholds, latency budget, and automated rollback trigger.

devon-eng: creating ticket PRD-4123 with logs and rollback plan. Will update thread when rollback is scheduled.

sam-sales: forwarding to Synapse and requesting patience. Will share ETA when we confirm. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment event: routing-config-update v2026.03.15 applied 02:10 UTC — triggered canary -> rolled to 12% of requests.

maria: good note — post-action: product to prioritize a small initiative for "Dedicated routing safety" (canary guardrails + per-customer routing pins) in next sprint. Scope: config UI for pins, automation for rollback, and metrics alerting. Acceptance: automated rollback fires <5 mins after threshold breach.

alex: agreed. For immediate next steps: (1) devon rollback now, (2) kevin apply temporary pool bump, (3) maria create PRD and notify CSM. devon please update ticket with ETA.

devon-eng: rollback scheduled now, I'll post confirmation when p95 drops.

sam-sales: copied. thanks team.

-- thread created by alex at 1765432100, last update 1765432190 --
